data.name: Mahshid
data.long_meaning: From the Persian word 'mahshid' meaning 'guide' or 'leader'. In Islamic culture, the name Mahshid represents a spiritual guide or a leader who shows the way to the right path. This name is also associated with wisdom and knowledge.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual guide or teacher leading the way to knowledge and wisdom.
data.numerology_meaning: People with the name Mahshid are independent, free-thinking, and driven by their inner desire for knowledge and wisdom. They have a strong sense of purpose and a natural ability to guide and lead others.

in_english.name: Mahshid
in_english.long_meaning: Mahshid is derived from the Arabic root (m-sh-d), which means to plan, prepare, and organize. In Islamic theology, the term refers to the paradise's sacred pasture, where believers will be rewarded with comfort and bliss. The name represents the concept of planning and organizing one's life according to the will of Allah. In Islamic tradition, Mahshid is associated with the concept of justice, fairness, and compassion. It is also linked to the idea of achieving spiritual growth and self-improvement through one's actions and deeds.

historical_references.context: Mahshid bint Amr ibn al-As was the wife of the Umayyad Caliph Muawiya I. She is described as a 'lady of great beauty and wisdom'. Mahshid played a pivotal role in the negotiations between Muawiya and Constantine III, the Byzantine Emperor, that led to the peace treaty between the two powers. This treaty allowed Muslims to trade freely in the Byzantine territories and facilitated the spread of Islam in Syria and beyond.
